newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude ease as traders battle over Brent.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude ease as traders battle over Brent.

text.p: North Sea crudes eased on Friday as a tussle between traders over the value of benchmark Dated Brent failed to mask a weak fundamental picture.
"There's an expensive loop and a cheap loop so we'll probably see deals miles apart on Monday," said a trader.
A Wall Street trader, who bought four Brents at quotes-related prices on Thursday, sold one but kept three more turning wet on Friday, traders said.
The March 1-3 cargo was sold for Mar Brent -13 cents to a trader who was also bidding Mar Brent -10 cents for another cargo in the March 1-12 period to fill a ULCC.
Brent loading March 6-8 traded at Mar -2 cents on Wednesday.
Shipping brokers said Glencore provisionally fixed the ULCC Kirsten loading four or five cargoes of Brent in the first decade of March for a trip to South Africa.
Traders said reduced output at some North Sea fields due to bad weather this week could provide a degree of support to spot differentials but there was still an overhang of prompt supply.

Two cross-month Oseberg cargoes were sold on Friday. Traders said the barrels probably moved at a small discount to Dated Brent after a similar cargo fetched Dated Brent +11 cents at the start of the week.
Statoil's 570,000 barrels per day (bpd) Gullfaks oilfield system was running at just 10 percent of capacity on Friday after bad weather prevented offshore loadings and storage reached capacity.
Elswhere, March 17-19 Forties fetched Dated Brent +38 cents, in line with a deal on Thursday but a March 12 Ekofisk was sold for Dated Brent +27 cents, down a couple of cents.

In the Mediterranean, spot offers of Iraqi Kirkuk and poor margins continued to pressure the sour crude market. Syria's Sytrol revised down its opening offer in March price talks to Dated Brent -32 cents but lifters stuck to -50/-45 cents.
